title: Source files
notes: One row per spreadsheet downloaded from the statistics pages of the Public Employment Services portal (MRPiPS n.d.). The full inventory with URL, download date and SHA-256 checksum is data/raw/mrpips/source_inventory.csv. Where MRPiPS revised a table (the 2021 tables republished in 2025), the superseded file is kept with use = 0 and is not read.

title: Annual documents by channel, 2008-2025 (data of Figure 1)
notes: Documents issued or registered during the year; not unique persons. NA: channel not yet in operation (seasonal permits before 2018, notifications before 2022). ZUS: stock of insured foreigners at the end of the year, as reported in MRPiPS (2026).
source: Authors' calculations based on MRPiPS registers; ZUS stock as reported in MRPiPS (2026).

title: Concentration series: effective number of origins (1/HHI) (data of Figure 3)
notes: HHI = sum of squared origin shares of documents. Annual totals except the half-yearly work-permit series (36 half-years). 'Declaration persons' replaces the number of declarations by the number of persons covered (available from 2019).
source: Authors' calculations based on MRPiPS registers.

title: Origins and estimation samples

parts.caption: All origins, with sample membership and reasons for exclusion

notes: Sample sizes refer to 2011-2025 (15 years). Origins without World Bank real GDP-per-capita growth data or with only zero outcomes are dropped from the fixed-effects models; all-zero origins are retained when origin effects are replaced by the pre-sample mean (Table 4). Comparison origins (Section 5.3): never eligible for declarations and at least 500 documents in 2008-2025.
source: Authors' calculations based on MRPiPS registers and World Bank (2026).

title: Policy coding: declaration access, EU visa freedom and shock indicators
notes: Access shares are the share of calendar days in the year on which the right applied (data/policy/access_spells.csv). EU visa freedom applies to holders of biometric passports. Group indicators equal one for the six declaration nationalities (ARM, BLR, GEO, MDA, RUS, UKR) from 2018 and from 2022.
source: Authors' compilation based on the legal acts listed (Dziennik Ustaw) and European Commission (2026).

title: Group difference in persistence: alternative inference
notes: Difference between the recent-flow elasticities of origins with and without declaration access (Table 3, column 3), estimated as a single coefficient. Only six origins ever have access, so all intervals are approximate. Pairs bootstrap: origins resampled with replacement; draws that contain no access origin do not identify the difference and are reported. Wild cluster score bootstrap: Kline and Santos (2012), null imposed, Rademacher and Webb weights; the interval is the set of null values not rejected at 5 percent.
source: Authors' estimates based on MRPiPS registers and World Bank (2026).

title: Additional persistence estimates by access group
notes: PPML with origin and year effects; standard errors clustered by origin in parentheses. Controls as in Table 3, column 3, unless stated. *** p<0.01, ** p<0.05, * p<0.1.
source: Authors' estimates based on MRPiPS registers and World Bank (2026).

title: Changes in declaration access: DiD summaries, event-study coefficients and placebo distributions

parts.caption: Event-study coefficients (reference year t-1) and placebo percentiles

notes: k = number of placebo estimates with an absolute value at least as large as the treated estimate; N = number of estimable placebo estimates. p = k/N is the convention used in the submitted version; p = (k+1)/(N+1) counts the treated unit. Georgia gained access in December 2010: results are shown with event year 0 = 2011 (first full year, Table 5) and 2010 (Figure 4 heading). The Armenian case is repeated with post-Soviet comparison origins only.
source: Authors' estimates based on MRPiPS registers.

title: Interrupted time series with standard errors
notes: Panel A: January 2021 - November 2025; Panel B: January 2015 - December 2019 (break January 2018) and half-yearly work permits 2015-2021 (time in years). OLS on log counts (log(1+y) for seasonal permits) with a linear trend and calendar-month effects; February 2022 pulse in Panel A. Newey-West standard errors (6 lags monthly, 2 lags half-yearly). Level changes in percent; slopes in log points per month. The June-November 2025 segment has six observations; slope changes are relative to the pre-break trend after calendar-month effects, so a positive slope change can coincide with a falling raw series.
source: Authors' estimates based on MRPiPS registers.

title: Duration-sensitive concentration
notes: Document-month weights use the maximum duration by channel and year (data/policy/document_duration.csv): permits 36, declarations 6 (24 from 2022), seasonal permits 9; notifications have no fixed maximum and the assumed weight is stated in that file. Holders: citizens holding a current work-authorising document on 31 December 2025.
source: Authors' calculations based on MRPiPS registers and MRPiPS (2026).

title: Applications and issuance, 2025
notes: Applications, pending cases and issued permits need not refer to the same cohorts. 'Origins without declaration or notification access': all origins except ARM, BLR, GEO, MDA, RUS and UKR.
source: MRPiPS (2025a, 2025b, 2026); authors' calculations based on MRPiPS registers.

title: Person-based benchmarks
notes: The populations and reference periods differ: documents issued in a year, holders of a current document at year end, and persons insured in ZUS. None of these figures validates another directly; residence-and-work permits are not deduplicated against the four registers.

title: Software and runtime
notes: Software versions are recorded at run time by code/10_appendix_tables.py; runtimes are taken from output/logs/runtime.csv.
